why_this_matters: Day 177 sits in Phase 10 (Machine Learning), whose goal is: Train, tune, evaluate and explain supervised models from first principles. Today's core material - Recursive binary splitting, Variance reduction criterion, Depth, min_samples and pruning - is the vocabulary the rest of the phase is built on. Learners who skip the concept and jump to copying code usually stall two weeks later; the goal here is that you can explain what you did, not just that it ran.

code.heading: ML Models with HyperParameter Tuning
code.code:
# creating a function to train and evaluate the models with the best parameters
def train_and_evaluate_best(model):
    model.fit(X_train, y_train)
    pred = model.predict(X_test)
    print(f"Accuracy Score: {accuracy_score(y_test, pred)}")
    print(f"Confusion Matrix: \n{confusion_matrix(y_test, pred)}")
    print(f"Classification Report: \n{classification_report(y_test, pred)}")

# Logistic Regression
print("Logistic Regression")
log_reg = LogisticRegression(C=10, penalty='l2')
train_and_evaluate_best(log_reg)

# Decision Tree
print("Decision Tree")
dt = DecisionTreeClassifier(criterion='entropy', max_depth=9)
train_and_evaluate_best(dt)

# Random Forest
print("Random Forest")
rf = RandomForestClassifier(criterion='entropy', max_depth=9, n_estimators=19)
train_and_evaluate_best(rf)

# Gradient Boosting
print("Gradient Boosting")
gb = GradientBoostingClassifier(learning_rate=0.1, max_depth=2, n_estimators=19)
train_and_evaluate_best(gb)

# XGBoost
print("XGBoost")
xgb = XGBClassifier(learning_rate=0.1,
                    max_depth=2,
                    n_estimators=19,
                    objective='binary:logistic',
                    use_label_encoder=False,
                    eval_metric='logloss')
train_and_evaluate_best(xgb)

# save the decision tree classifier
from sklearn.tree import export_graphviz
export_graphviz(model, out_file='./saved_models/Decision_tree_03.dot', feature_names=X.columns, filled=True, rounded=True)

# create and train teh model with pred
model = DecisionTreeClassifier(criterion='entropy', random_state=42)
model.fit(X_train, y_train)

# predict the model
y_pred = model.predict(X_test)
# evaluate the model
print(confusion_matrix(y_test, y_pred))
print(classification_report(y_test, y_pred))

common_mistakes.mistake: Watching the lecture without running the repository notebook.
common_mistakes.why: Recognition is not recall: code that looked obvious fails the moment you type it yourself.
common_mistakes.fix: For every topic today, run the linked notebook cell, then retype it from memory in your own file.

common_mistakes.mistake: Using Recursive binary splitting on data whose types or shape you have not printed.
common_mistakes.why: Most failures in this topic are input problems (dtype, shape, missing values) rather than logic errors.
common_mistakes.fix: Print type and shape immediately before the operation; keep that habit for all 275 days.

debugging.symptom: The linked notebook cell raises ModuleNotFoundError or ImportError.
debugging.cause: Wrong kernel/environment selected, or the library is not installed in the active environment.
debugging.fix: Print sys.executable in the notebook and install into that environment (Day 4).

debugging.symptom: Your output differs from the recording even though the code looks identical.
debugging.cause: Library version differences, a changed default argument, or unseeded randomness.
debugging.fix: Pin versions (requirements.txt), set a random seed, and compare dtypes and shapes, not just values (Day 5).

real_world: Roles that use Recursive binary splitting daily: data analyst, data scientist and ML engineer. In industry the tool matters less than the judgement about when to use it - that judgement is what interviews and performance reviews reward.
